title: Find the short foot of a rocking motor base and shim only that foot
instruction: Shim the motor base so it sits level and solid on all four feet, then let go.
context: Millwrights and industrial machinery mechanics check a motor base for soft foot before alignment: if one foot is off the baseplate, the base rocks and bolting it down twists the frame. They pack only that foot; a shim under the wrong one will not go in or leaves the motor tilted. Done by: millwrights and industrial machinery mechanics. Unlike TK-UEK6R4 (raise a baseplate on wedges) and TK-QXR5CL (the instruction names the rocking board and cause), nothing says which foot is short.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Baseplate (fixed, grey painted steel): 38 cm front to back, 24 cm wide, 1.5 cm thick, centred on the midline 26.0 cm in front of the arm bases (it spans 7.0 to 45.0 cm). Scribe marks (fixed, dark, 2 mm wide, 0.5 mm proud of the baseplate): two lines 10 cm long running front to back, centred 30.0 cm in front, 7.5 cm left and 7.5 cm right of the midline, and one line 8 cm long across the midline at 40.5 cm in front. Motor base (loose, one rigid piece, 1.5 kg): a dark painted steel frame 20 cm front to back, 14 cm wide and 5 cm tall, centred on the midline 30.0 cm in front, standing on four square foot pads 3 x 3 cm, one under each corner with its outer sides flush with the frame's sides. Three pads are 10 mm tall; the near-left pad is 5 mm tall. The base starts resting level on the other three, its frame underside 1.0 cm above the baseplate and a 5 mm gap under the near-left pad. On the frame lies a blue motor, a cylinder 7 cm across and 10 cm long, its axis front to back, centred 5.0 cm in front of and 3.5 cm right of the frame's centre. A silver shaft, 16 mm across and 3 cm long, comes out of the motor's far end. The density is even throughout, which puts the centre of mass about 11 mm in front of and 8 mm right of the frame's centre. Shim (loose, one piece, 100 g): a steel plate 10 cm front to back, 5 cm wide and 4.2 mm thick, with an orange plastic tab block 1.5 cm front to back, 5 cm wide and 3 cm tall at its near end. It lies flat on the baseplate, centred on the midline 13.5 cm in front (the plate spans 8.5 to 18.5 cm), tab toward the robot. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Pass/fail. A foot's gap is the height of the centre of its pad's underside above what it stands on: the shim's top if the shim covers at least 75% of that pad's area, seen from above, otherwise the baseplate. A feeler gauge or a ruler at the pad measures it. Score 1.0 when, with the robot clear: the shim lies flat on the baseplate (tilted at most 2 degrees, underside within 1 mm of the plate); no pad is between 2% and 75% covered by the shim; every foot's gap is at most 1.0 mm and none of them sinks more than 0.5 mm below its surface; the base is level within 0.5 degrees (spirit level on the frame); the base's centre is within 3 mm of its starting position and its turn within 2 degrees, shaft still pointing away from the robot (check against the scribe marks); and base and shim are still. The trial ends at 1.0 once this has held for 1 s. Score 0 in every other case: no shim, a shim part-way under, under a foot that already bears, or under the far-right foot, which stops the rock but tilts the base about 2.6 degrees; the base held down; the base moved or turned off its marks.
reset_notes: Pull the shim out and lay it back flat at its start, tab toward the robot. Set the motor base back on its scribe marks, shaft away from the robot, resting on its three long feet. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, bench scale: the foot is 5 mm short and the shim leaves 0.8 mm. Real soft foot is often under 0.1 mm, found with a feeler gauge as each hold-down bolt is loosened; here the base is checked unbolted, as before bolting, and 1.0 mm is a simulation tolerance. One fixed shim thickness. Fixed layout: the same foot is short every trial, marked only by its gap. Even-density parts; friction 1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic.
